questions.stem: Why is the lagging strand synthesized discontinuously?

options.A: DNA polymerase synthesizes only in the 5′→3′ direction
options.B: Helicase unwinds only the lagging-strand template
options.C: Primase can prime only the leading strand
options.D: DNA polymerase reads the template only 5′→3′
options.E: Ligase must seal each fragment before the next begins

questions.explanation: Polymerase adds nucleotides only to a 3′ end (synthesis 5′→3′), so the strand oriented against fork movement is made in Okazaki fragments. B: Helicase unwinds both strands. C: Every new strand needs a primer. D: Polymerase reads the template 3′→5′. E: Ligase joins the fragments afterward.

questions.stem: In which order are RNA primers handled at the end of DNA replication?

options.A: Ligase → RNase H → DNA polymerase I
options.B: RNase H → DNA polymerase I → ligase
options.D: RNase H → DNA polymerase III → topoisomerase
options.E: DNA polymerase I → RNase H → ligase

questions.explanation: Per the lecture: RNase H removes the primers, DNA polymerase I fills the gaps, DNA ligase seals the nicks. A: Nicks can't be sealed before primers are replaced. C: Primase makes primers; it doesn't remove them. D: Topoisomerase relieves supercoiling; it doesn't seal nicks. E: Primers must be removed before pol I fills the gap.

questions.stem: A template DNA strand reads 3′-TACGGA-5′. What is the mRNA sequence?
questions.explanation: RNA is complementary to the template and antiparallel, matching the coding strand (5′-ATGCCT-3′) with U for T. A: That's the template itself. B: Reversed. C: Uses T, so it's DNA. E: Wrong orientation.

questions.stem: A mutation changes the intron's first two nucleotides from GU to AU. What is the most likely consequence?

options.C: Abnormal splicing at the donor site
options.D: Premature stop codon in the exon

questions.explanation: GU marks the 5′ (donor) splice site; altering it disrupts splicing (exon skipping or intron retention). A: Capping is independent of splice sites. B: AAUAAA is the poly(A) signal. D: Not a coding change. E: Kozak surrounds the start codon.

questions.stem: Which enzyme ensures each tRNA carries the correct amino acid?
questions.explanation: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases attach each amino acid to its tRNA. A: Peptidyl transferase forms peptide bonds. C: RNA pol III transcribes tRNA genes. D: Release factors end translation. E: Poly(A) polymerase adds the tail.

questions.stem: During elongation, where does an incoming aminoacyl-tRNA bind?
questions.explanation: New aminoacyl-tRNAs enter the A site; the growing chain sits in the P site; empty tRNAs exit from the E site. A: P holds the peptidyl-tRNA. B: E is the exit. D: Cap binding happens at initiation. E: Kozak is an mRNA sequence.

questions.stem: A mutation in the AAUAAA sequence of a gene's 3′ region would most directly impair which step?

options.D: Transcription initiation at the TATA box
options.E: Cleavage and polyadenylation of the pre-mRNA

questions.explanation: AAUAAA signals the endonuclease to cleave and poly(A) polymerase to add the tail. A: Capping is at the 5′ end. B: Branch points are within introns. C: AUG is the start codon. D: TATA is in the promoter.

questions.stem: A point variant changes the codon UGG (Trp) to UGA. What happens when the ribosome reaches this codon?

options.A: A release factor recognizes it and the chain is released
options.B: A tRNA reads UGA as tryptophan by wobble pairing
options.C: The ribosome skips the codon and continues
options.D: A different amino acid is inserted
options.E: Translation continues to the normal stop codon

questions.explanation: UGA is a stop codon (with UAA and UAG); release factors recognize it, water is added instead of a peptide bond, and a truncated protein is released. B: Wobble lets a tRNA read synonymous sense codons; no tRNA reads stop codons. C: Stop codons end translation; they aren't skipped. D: Stop codons don't encode amino acids. E: Translation ends at the new stop codon.

questions.stem: During DNA replication, the error rate falls from about 1 in 10⁴ to about 1 in 10⁸ nucleotides. Which activity is mainly responsible during replication?

options.B: Gap filling by DNA polymerase I

questions.explanation: Per the lecture, DNA polymerase III proofreads during replication, and pol II corrects remaining errors at the end. A: RNase H removes RNA primers. B: Pol I fills gaps left by primers. C: Ligase seals nicks. E: Helicase breaks hydrogen bonds to open the fork.
